findings.finding: The AC promises a skew report for any gate run whose attested config names a model the local code cannot drive. The implementation only reports when ancestry PROVES the running build is a strict ancestor of the pinned SHA. detect_drift returns None, so nothing is reported, when the build has diverged from the pinned SHA (`_is_ancestor` is false). That is the usual case for a worktree branch with its own commits off an older main. It also returns None when build provenance or git data is unavailable. The plan's title targets 'stale worktrees', but a stale worktree with local commits gets no skew note and still shows only the provider 400.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC 1 / Expected section; src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py:130-175
scenarios: A feature branch forked from 49f5d6d0580 with two local commits runs review-plan after main moves to 5.5. The build has diverged from origin/main and is not an ancestor, so coverage.build_drift is absent and only the provider 400 shows
A wheel install without _build_info.COMMIT: no build SHA, so the note never appears

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define skew as 'the attested SHA has commits not in the running build' (count `build..pinned` from the merge-base), not strict ancestry, so diverged feature-branch worktrees are also reported. Add a test for the diverged case.
evidence: Context: 'every worktree still on the older code fails its gates'
src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py:158-159 `if not _is_ancestor(build_full, pinned_full, root): return None  # ahead of, or diverged from, the pinned ref`
Observed repro used a worktree at `49f5d6d0580`, the exact parent of `06b3b1a5230`, so it was a strict ancestor
findings.finding: The plan doesn't define skew for the most common stale-worktree shape: a feature-branch worktree with local commits on an older base. That worktree has diverged from origin/main rather than being a strict ancestor of it. A strict-ancestry check like the existing `detect_drift` (which returns None for 'ahead of, or diverged from') stays silent there, even though the worktree lacks the capability rows main added. The observed case happened to be at the exact parent commit, which hides this gap.
scenarios: A developer's ticket worktree has 3 local commits on a main from last week. Main moves models, and the gate fails with the same bare provider 400 and no skew note.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat drift as proven when `git rev-list --count <build>..<pinned>` > 0 and both SHAs exist in the target repo, whether or not the build is a strict ancestor. Word the remedy as 'merge/rebase onto <pinned> and `make install`'.

evidence: AC: 'names a model the local code cannot drive'
Context: the 5.5 model ID was simply absent from the old _MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES; an unknown model falls through to defaults (temperature sent)
findings.finding: The detection signal for 'a model the local code cannot drive' is undefined. Older capability tables by definition have no knowledge of the new model, so the local code cannot tell from its own tables that it is missing an override. The plan does not say whether skew is detected by comparing versions, by re-attributing a provider 400 after the fact, or by checking that the model ID is unknown.
scenarios: An 'unknown model ID' heuristic fires for every brand-new model, even when the local code can drive it fine (false positive).
A pure '400 then attribute to skew' heuristic mislabels a genuine provider or config error as skew whenever the attested SHA differs from local.
findings.suggested_fix: Define skew as follows: the attested commit that last touched [tool.rebar.llm] is not an ancestor of the locally installed rebar build commit. Check this before the LLM call. Optionally, only when a provider ValidationException occurs, upgrade the error to a skew diagnosis.

findings.finding: The plan does not specify how the gate decides that the local code 'cannot drive' the attested model. Older code has no override row for a newer model and applies default capabilities, so it cannot recognize the model as unsupported from its own tables. Detection must come from one of three sources: comparing the attested SHA to the local code version, a capability/version marker in the attested snapshot, or classifying the provider 400 after it happens. None is chosen, so the core mechanism is left to the implementer.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define 'local code version' as the installed rebar package version/build SHA (not the cwd worktree), and make the remedy shape-aware: upgrade the installed rebar, with 'update the worktree + make install' only when running from a rebar source checkout.
evidence: "naming the attested SHA, the local code version, and the remedy: update the worktree and `make install`"
The observed fix was `git merge --ff-only origin/main` plus `make install` inside the rebar repo itself.
findings.finding: The remedy text and the 'local code version' it reports assume rebar is running from a rebar source worktree with a Makefile. For a consumer that installs rebar as a package and runs gates against its own target repo, the attested config comes from that repo's origin/main and the local code is the installed rebar wheel. 'Update the worktree and `make install`' is wrong advice there, and a git-SHA-based local version is not available.
findings.location: Expected — "the remedy: update the worktree and `make install`"
scenarios: Target project = Ruby (or .NET) monorepo using the rebar CLI installed from a package: its config names a newer model, and the gate tells the user to update their worktree and run `make install`. Their repo has no such target, and updating it does not change the installed rebar, so the skew persists.

Remote MCP server outside the checkout: the server's installed rebar has no worktree git SHA, so the 'local code version' is missing or wrong in the report, and 'update the worktree' does not apply to the server's install.
findings.suggested_fix: Report the installed rebar version from package metadata (e.g. importlib.metadata) plus the build SHA if embedded. Phrase the remedy as 'upgrade rebar to a version at or after <attested SHA>' and add the make-install hint only when the install is an editable rebar checkout.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Restate AC 1's trigger as a provenance check: the running build commit (from `running_build_sha`) is behind the attested `verified_at_sha`. Name `build_drift.detect_drift` / `degraded_verdict_note` as the mechanism instead of 'a model the local code cannot drive'.

findings.finding: The AC's trigger, 'attested config names a model the local code cannot drive', is not something the executing (older) code can decide. By definition that code has no rows for models introduced after it, and unknown models normally fall back to family defaults and run fine. The plan never names the signal the gate uses to detect skew. The only sound signal is build provenance: is the running build's commit a strict ancestor of the attested SHA? That is decidable without knowing the new model.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC 1 ('names a model the local code cannot drive')
scenarios: A future config moves to a model id that the old code's tables don't mention. Old code can't know it 'cannot drive' it, so a model-keyed detector never fires.
An implementer adds a 'known models' allowlist check. It flags every unmeasured-but-working model as skew and misses skew that involves known models with changed capability rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword AC 1: 'When the running rebar build is proven behind the attested SHA (build_drift.detect_drift) and the model never ran (`coverage.llm_ran is false`), the verdict carries `coverage.build_drift` naming build SHA, attested SHA, commits behind, and the remedy (ff-merge origin/main + `make install`).'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin AC 1 with a test that fakes the running build SHA as a strict ancestor of the attested SHA and forces a model-never-ran verdict (`llm_ran: false`), then asserts `coverage.build_drift` names both SHAs and the update/`make install` remedy. Add a negative case where the build is at or ahead of the attested SHA.

findings.finding: The test the AC requires ('pairs a newer attested config with older capability tables') pins a proxy, not the detection mechanism. The skew note is driven by git ancestry plus `llm_ran: false`, not by capability tables. And under current opt-in sampling (`_SAMPLING_ACCEPTING_MODEL_IDS` + `SamplingRetryModel`), an unmeasured model is never sent `temperature`, so 'older capability tables' no longer reproduce the observed 400 on their own. A test built that way either fails to provoke the failure or passes without exercising the skew detector.
scenarios: The test swaps in older capability rows, the model call succeeds (no temperature sent), `llm_ran` is true, and the test proves nothing about skew reporting.
The detector regresses (e.g. the ancestry probe breaks), but a capability-table-shaped test still passes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in the plan whether skew on a run where the model DID run should also be surfaced in the verdict (e.g. `coverage.build_drift` added whenever drift is proven), or explicitly scope it out with a one-line reason.

findings.finding: The plan scopes reporting to runs that fail outright. Skew that silently produces a wrong-but-completed run is left unaddressed and unacknowledged. The same commit class also changes `effort` and structured-output rows, and older code would run the model with the wrong settings without failing. The Expected says the gate 'detects the skew and says so', but the AC only covers the failing-call path.
scenarios: An older build runs a 5.5 model without the pinned `effort`. The gate returns a signed verdict at a different reasoning effort, with no visible skew notice beyond a log warning.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add one or two sentences saying why detect-and-report is the chosen approach (old builds can't learn new model rows; build provenance vs attested SHA is decidable and fails open) and drop the 'either ... or' wording from Expected.

No sentence explains why the detect-and-report option was chosen
findings.finding: The plan gives no positive rationale for its chosen approach. Expected offers two remedies (report the skew, or resolve capabilities from the config that was read), and the AC adopts reporting without saying why it fits. For example: the old build can't be patched retroactively, provenance is decidable without model knowledge, and loading capability data from the attested snapshot would widen the attested-input trust surface.
scenarios: An implementer reads 'either ... or' and builds the snapshot-sourced capability resolution instead, which is a larger and riskier change than the AC requires.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace Expected with: 'A gate run whose running build is behind the attested SHA says so in the verdict (attested SHA, build SHA, remedy). Provenance is chosen because an older build cannot know a newer model's capabilities, while git ancestry between the two SHAs is decidable and fails open.'

src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:268-275: sampling is opt-in, and every model 'nobody has measured, are absent and run at their provider's default sampling'. So 'model id missing from the local tables' is the normal path, not a skew signal.

Absence from the capability tables cannot be the signal, because the code deliberately leaves unmeasured model ids out of those tables and runs them at provider defaults.

Rewrite the AC test to pin 'older build SHA + newer pinned SHA + model never ran ⇒ note present' rather than comparing capability tables.

The repo already uses a concrete shape: src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py:242-254 returns {build_sha, build_date, pinned_sha, commits_behind, dirty, remedy}, attached as `coverage["build_drift"]` by gate_source.py:261-272. The plan neither adopts nor references it.
findings.finding: The plan does not say where the skew report goes in the gate verdict or what fields it has. The Effects section complains that 'no finding names the cause', yet the plan never decides whether the fix is a finding, a new `coverage` key, or a change to the verdict. It also leaves open whether the verdict stays an unsigned INDETERMINATE, and what form 'the local code version' takes.
findings.location: Expected section ("naming the attested SHA, the local code version, and the remedy"); AC 1 ("reports the version skew")
scenarios: One implementer emits a finding and another adds a coverage key. Tools that parse gate verdicts cannot rely on either.
'Local code version' gets reported as the package version string. That cannot be compared with the attested git SHA, so the operator cannot tell how far behind they are.
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt the existing contract: attach `coverage["build_drift"]` with keys build_sha, build_date, pinned_sha, commits_behind, dirty, and remedy (the remedy text names `git merge --ff-only origin/main` and `make install`). Keep `coverage.llm_error` unchanged, keep the verdict unsigned INDETERMINATE, and don't add a finding.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the fallback for unprovable skew (unknown build SHA, no pinned SHA, git unavailable, diverged history, probe error): report nothing, leave verdict and signature unchanged, never raise.
evidence: The plan covers only the case where skew is present, and never says what the gate emits when skew is unknowable.

The code already has to make this choice: src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py:1-6 says missing provenance, missing git data, unrelated repos, and probe errors all 'fail open without changing the verdict or signature'. The plan states no such contract.
findings.finding: The plan gives no fallback for when skew cannot be proven. This covers an unknown build SHA (non-editable install without baked commit metadata), a local-source gate with no pinned SHA, git being unavailable, or a build that has diverged from the pinned ref instead of falling behind it. It also doesn't say whether a failure in the skew probe may change the verdict.
scenarios: A wheel install without `_build_info.COMMIT`: does the gate stay silent, report 'skew unknown', or fail?
A worktree that has diverged from origin/main (neither ahead nor behind): is that skew?
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Expected: 'When the build SHA or pinned SHA is unknown, git is unavailable, the histories diverge, or the probe raises, no skew note is emitted and the verdict and signature are unchanged (fail-open, advisory only).'
